issue: Effect of court-sanctioned amalgamation on tenancy transfer and possible eviction or assignment consequences under Delhi rent control law
act: Delhi Rent Control Act, s. 14(1)(b), in the context of a court-sanctioned company amalgamation
date_scope: Judgment dated 5 December 1980; no broader historical version of the Rent Control Act is supplied
procedure_scope: Company scheme-sanction stage; the court states a prima facie view on vesting but expressly leaves eviction or actionable-assignment consequences for the appropriate rent-control or civil proceeding

conditions.text: Prima facie, contractual or statutory tenancy rights of the transferor company are transferable on amalgamation by the court's vesting order, without landlord consent, and fall outside s. 14(1)(b)
conditions.quote: Prima facie, the rights of the transferor-company in the tenancy, contractual or statutory, are transferable on an amalgamation by virtue of the vesting order to be made by the court while sanctioning the scheme of amalgamation or thereafter and having regard to the nature of such a vesting it would not require the consent of the landlord and would be outside the mischief of the provisions of s. 14(1)(b) of the Rent Control Act.

conditions.text: The court did not decide at this stage whether such transfer nevertheless amounts to an assignment that could support eviction under s. 14(1)(b) or a regular civil action
conditions.quote: This court is, however, not concerned at this stage if the transfer by or consequent on amalgamation by the order of the court would nevertheless be tantamount to the assignment of a tenancy and if without the consent of the landlord would render the company or the transferee-company liable to eviction under s. 14(1)(b) of the Rent Control Act or otherwise be actionable in a regular civil action against them.

conditions.text: Any such assignment or eviction question must be examined in the special jurisdiction created by the Rent Control Act or in a maintainable regular civil action
conditions.quote: Such a matter has to be examined and decided in accordance with the special jurisdiction created by that Act or on a regular civil action, if maintainable.

conditions.text: No landlord cause of action accrues before amalgamation and consequential vesting; any cause of action follows those events
conditions.quote: No cause of action accrues to the landlord before the amalgamation and consequential vesting. The cause of action, if any, follows the amalgamation and the vesting.

conditions.text: If an assignment in law attracts the Delhi Rent Control Act, the landlord remains free to proceed under that Act or by regular civil action before the appropriate authority
conditions.quote: If there is any assignment in law, which may attract the provisions of the Delhi Rent Control Act, the landlord would be free to take recourse to the proceedings under that Act or in a regular civil action and such proceedings would be dealt with and decided by the appropriate authority in accordance with law.

limitations: The source characterizes the tenancy-transfer proposition only as prima facie.
The core s. 14(1)(b) eviction or assignment question is expressly reserved and not finally adopted in this passage.
The supplied unit is a partial judicial document, not a complete statement of Delhi rent-control law.

date_scope: Supplied official consolidation is identified as amended through 2021, with historical-version applicability unverified; amendment notes shown in the text include changes from 1950, 1960, 1961, and 1963
procedure_scope: Voluntary banking-company amalgamation under s. 44A, including shareholder approval, meeting notice, dissenting-shareholder rights, Reserve Bank sanction, and vesting consequences

conditions.text: A banking company may be amalgamated with another banking company only if a draft scheme is placed before each company's shareholders and approved by a majority in number representing two-thirds in value of those present in person or by proxy
conditions.quote:
no 
banking company shall be amalgamated with another banking company, unless a 
scheme containing the terms of such amalgamation has been placed in draft before 
the shareholders of each of the banking companies concerned separately, and 
approved by a resolution passed by a majority in number representing two- thirds 
in value of the shareholders of each of the said companies, present either in person 
or by proxy at a meeting called for the purpose.

conditions.text: Notice of the approval meeting must be given to every shareholder under the articles and must also be published weekly for three consecutive weeks in at least two qualifying local newspapers, one in a commonly understood local language
conditions.quote:
Notice of every such meeting as is referred to in sub-section (1) shall be given 
to every shareholder of each of the banking companies concerned in accordance 
with the relevant articles of association indicating the time, place and object of the 
meeting, and shall also be published at least once a week for three consecutive 
weeks in not less than two newspapers which circulate in the locality or localities 
where the registered offices of the banking companies concerned are situated, one 
of such newspapers being in a language commonly understood in the locality or 
localities.

sanctioned by the Reserve Bank, to claim from the banking company concerned, in 
respect of the shares held b y him in that company, their value as determined by 
the Reserve Bank when sanctioning the scheme

conditions.text: After the requisite shareholder approval, the scheme must be submitted to the Reserve Bank; a written Reserve Bank sanction makes it binding on the banking companies and all shareholders
conditions.quote:

shareholders in accordance with the provisions of this section, it shall be submitted 
to the Reserve Bank for sanction and shall, if sanctioned by the Reserve Bank by 
an order in writing passed  in this behalf, be binding on the banking companies 
concerned and also on all the shareholders thereof.

conditions.text: On Reserve Bank sanction, the amalgamated bank's property vests in, and its liabilities become liabilities of, the acquiring banking company, subject to the sanctioned scheme

properly of the amalgamated banking company shall, by virtue of the order of

banking company which under the scheme of amalgamation is to acquire the 
business of the amalgamated banking company, subject in all cases to  
3[the

issue: Lawfulness and consent requirements for subletting or transfer of tenancy rights
date_scope: The supplied text distinguishes subletting before 9 June 1952, subletting on or after 9 June 1952, and conduct after commencement of the Act; the commencement date itself is not supplied.
procedure_scope: Substantive statutory treatment of subletting, assignment, and landlord consent; no target-case judicial interpretation is supplied.

conditions.text: A subletting made before 9 June 1952 is deemed lawful despite lack of landlord consent if the sub-tenant is in occupation at commencement of the Act.
conditions.quote: (1) Where at any time before the 9th day of June, 1952, a tenant has sub-let the whole or any part of the premises and the sub-tenant is, at the commencement of this Act, in occupation of such premises, then notwithstanding that the consent of the landlord was not obtained for such sub-letting, the premises shall be deemed to have been lawfully sub-let.

conditions.text: A subletting made on or after 9 June 1952 without the landlord's written consent is not deemed lawful.
conditions.quote: (2) No premises which have been sub-let either in whole or in part on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord, shall be deemed to have been lawfully sub-let.

conditions.text: After commencement of the Act, a tenant may neither sublet nor transfer or assign tenancy rights without the landlord's previous written consent.
conditions.quote: (3) After the commencement of this Act, no tenant shall, without the previous consent in writing of the landlord, -(a) sub-let the whole or any part of the premises held by him as a tenant; or(b) transfer or assign his rights in the tenancy or in any part thereof.

conditions.text: A landlord may not demand or receive a premium, pugree, or other consideration for consenting to subletting.
conditions.quote: (4) No landlord shall claim or receive the payment of any sum as premium or pugree or claim or receive any consideration whatsoever in cash or in kind for giving his consent to the sub-letting of the whole or any part of the premises held by the tenant.

issue: notice and dispute procedure for sub-tenancy
date_scope: Distinguishes sub-letting after commencement of the Act from lawful sub-letting before commencement; creation and termination notices have specified one-month or six-month periods.
procedure_scope: Tenant or sub-tenant may give prescribed notice to the landlord; for contested pre-Act lawful sub-letting, landlord or sub-tenant may apply to the Controller within the specified two-month period, and the Controller decides the dispute.

conditions.text: For post-commencement sub-letting, the premises must have been sub-let in whole or part with the landlord's previous written consent.
conditions.quote: after the commencement of this Act, any premises are sub-let either in whole or in part by the tenant with the previous consent in writing of the landlord

conditions.text: For post-commencement sub-letting, the tenant or sub-tenant may give prescribed notice of creation within one month of sub-letting and notify termination within one month of termination.
conditions.quote: give notice to the landlord of the creation of the sub-tenancy within one month of the date of such sub-letting and notify the termination of such sub- tenancy within one month of such termination

conditions.text: For pre-commencement lawful sub-letting, the tenant or sub-tenant may give prescribed notice of creation within six months of commencement and notify termination within one month of termination.
conditions.quote: before the commencement of this Act, any premises have been lawfully sub-let either in whole or in part by the tenant

conditions.text: If the landlord contests lawful sub-letting in a case under subsection (2), an application by the landlord or sub-tenant must be made to the Controller within two months of the relevant notice event for the Controller to decide the dispute.
conditions.quote: the landlord contests that the premises were not lawfully sub-let, and an application is made to the Controller in this behalf, either by the landlord or by the sub-tenant, within two months of the date of the receipt of the notice of sub-letting by the landlord or the issue of the notice by the tenant or the sub-tenant

issue: direct tenancy status of protected sub-tenants
date_scope: Subsection (1) operates from the date of a section 14 eviction order; subsection (2) covers tenant interests determined before commencement of the Act and operates from the date of commencement.
procedure_scope: Specifies when a qualifying sub-tenant is deemed to become a tenant holding directly under the landlord and the terms of that deemed tenancy.

conditions.text: An eviction order under section 14 must be made against the tenant but not against the sub-tenant referred to in section 17.
conditions.quote: an order for eviction in respect of any premises is made under section 14 against a tenant but not against a sub-tenant referred to in section 17

conditions.text: Notice of the sub-tenancy must have been given to the landlord.
conditions.quote: a notice of the sub-tenancy has been given to the landlord

conditions.text: When the subsection (1) conditions are met, the sub-tenant becomes a direct tenant from the date of the eviction order for the premises occupied, on the same terms and conditions the tenant would have had if the tenancy continued.
conditions.quote: the sub-tenant shall, with effect from the date of the order, be deemed to become a tenant holding directly under the landlord in respect of the premises in his occupation on the same terms and conditions on which the tenant would have held from the landlord, if the tenancy had continued

conditions.text: For the pre-commencement route, the tenant's interest must have been determined before commencement without determining the interest of a sub-tenant to whom the premises had been lawfully sub-let.
conditions.quote: before the commencement of this Act, the interest of a tenant in respect of any premises has been determined without determining the interest of any sub-tenant to whom the premises either in whole or in part had been lawfully sub-let

conditions.text: When the subsection (2) condition is met, the sub-tenant is deemed from commencement of the Act to hold directly under the landlord on the same terms and conditions the tenant would have had if the tenancy continued.
conditions.quote: the sub-tenant shall, with effect from the date of the commencement of this Act, be deemed to have become a tenant holding directly under the landlord on the same terms and conditions on which the tenant would have held from the landlord, if the tenancy had continued
